Hayao Miyazaki - Wikipedia

This is a Wikipedia biography of Hayao Miyazaki (born January 5, 1941, Tokyo City), the Japanese animator, filmmaker and manga artist who co-founded Studio Ghibli in 1985 and serves as its honorary chairman, and who is widely regarded as one of the greatest filmmakers in the history of animation. The article traces his career from joining Toei Animation in 1963 as an inbetween and key animator, through co-directing Lupin the Third Part I with Isao Takahata and directing his first feature The Castle of Cagliostro (1979) and the Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind manga and 1984 film, to the Ghibli classics Laputa: Castle in the Sky, My Neighbor Totoro, Kiki's Delivery Service, Porco Rosso, and Princess Mononoke—the first animated film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year. It also covers Spirited Away (2001), which won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and became Japan's highest-grossing film, his later works up to The Boy and the Heron (2023), his recurring themes (humanity's relationship with nature and technology, art and craftsmanship, pacifism, strong female protagonists), and his honors including Person of Cultural Merit (2012), the Academy Honorary Award (2014) and the Ramon Magsaysay Award (2024).

Source: Hayao Miyazaki - Wikipedia
